newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 18.

text.p: New Zealand's macho male image is killing young people through suicide, according to Nelson coroner Iam Smith, who is doing a study into the growing number of such deaths. Page 1.

Talks to find a coalition government are set to begin next week with New Zealand First opening negotiations with National on Monday and with Labour on Wednesday. The talks would be held at a neutral venue, likely to be in Parliament. NZ First leader Winston Peters said preliminiary talks would concentrate on procedural matters, such as confidentiality and the negotiating process. Page 1.

Christian Democrat leader Graeme Lee wandered the corridors of power for the last time yesterday, saying he was leaving Parliament with regrets but a great sense of achievement. He was ousted from Parliamnet at last Saturday's election. Page 2.

Public interst in the Cook Islands tax commission of inquiry in Auckland has fallen off and the pace of the inquiry has slowed. The public gallery has emptied except for a couple of interested Inland Revenue Department officials and a Fay Richwhite executive who pops in to check on progress. Page 2.
The financially stressed airforce was looking toward privatisation for relief, acting chief of air staff David Hill said on Thursday. Page 2.

The Government focused on Thursday on falls in the number of long-term registered unemployed after figures issued by the Employment Service showed a rises over the year. The September registered-unemployed figure of 154,133 was down 195 on the August figure, but 5,274 up on September 1995. Page 2.

ECNZ yesterday again proved itself in the Government's champion cash cow, handing over $461 million to the Crown from its latest financial year. This included $243 million in ordinary dividends and $218 million in tax in the June year. ECNZ confirmed its intention to pass a further special dividend of about $158 million to the Crown on March 31 1997 after a $655 million upward valuation of assets. Page 10.

Two of the country's biggest financial institutions, National Mutual and AMP, confirmed their faith in New Zealand investments before the election, despite predictions of market gloom if a left-wing government gained power. AMP moved about four percent of its funds into shares shortly before the election, taking money out of cash. NMFM said political concerns did not deter it from more than the usual level of money in New Zealand shares and bonds during the September quarter. Page 10.
Works Corporation made a final profit in the year to June of $16 million, the state owned enterprise saiys in its annual report issued on Thursday. Page 10.
Business confidence recovered lost ground in the September quarter, according to the latest survey by the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research. Page 10.
The Bankers Association has retained consumer liability provisions in its code of practice despite criticisms from the Consumer Affairs Ministry. Page 11.

High "spikes" in North Island wholesale electricity prices on Tuesday and Wednesday this week were unlikely to affect consumers, market operator EMCO chief executive Lincoln Gould said on Thursday. Page 11.
